summary: Designed and converged on a new extensions model for Gizmo: Gizmo ships with zero bundled extensions; a single registry git repo (curated by the user) is cloned once into a source home, built locally, and individual extensions are linked (symlinks on macOS/Linux, junctions on Windows) into the global pi extensions directory as paired .ts + .web.js files. Existing sibling-bundle UI serving and per-extension build isolation carry over unchanged.
decisions: Gizmo ships zero extensions at install time — no static web builtins, no seeded pi-extensions. All extensions arrive via the registry mechanism.
The registry is user-curated, not npm or any third-party index. The user owns the registry repo and the hosting.
The registry is structured as a single git repo (monorepo of extensions) cloned into ~/.pi/agent/extensions-src/registry/, not per-extension repos.
Install = link (symlink on macOS/Linux, directory junction on Windows so no admin rights needed); uninstall = remove link. Clone stays.
Update = git pull + rebuild; links need no touch since they point into the registry's build output.
Build output layout: build/<name>.ts + build/<name>.web.js, produced by a per-extension loop so one failed extension doesn't block the others.
The existing pi-extensions/ workspace in this repo becomes the dev home / source for publishing the registry (this repo can itself be the registry, cloned directly).
Gizmo's server role stays generic: manage clone home, invoke the registry's declared build, create/remove links, list status. No extension-specific knowledge.
